newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS IS ALL BUSINESS DESPITE MASTERS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS IS ALL BUSINESS DESPITE MASTERS LEAD.

text.p: While the golf world focused on Tiger Woods on Friday the young phenomenon focused on his golf game.

After the 21-year-old sensation put on a spectacular display of power golf to take the second-round lead in the Masters in only his third visit to Augusta National Golf Club, he went straight to the practice tee to work on his game -- leaving the world's news media cooling their heels with deadlines waiting.

Although he has been a professional golfer for only about eight months, the three-time U.S. Amateur champion was all business after outplaying the world's best golfers to hold a three-stroke lead halfway through the first major championship of the year.

Asked why he went to hit balls after producing a ball-striking exhibition that prompted standing ovations by the Masters' very astute galleries, the former Stanford University student-golfer said matter of factly, "I can always get better."
Woods reminded reporters that the tournament was only half over and he still had a long way to go before he could claim the first of what most people believe will be many, many major titles.
"This is only Friday," he said. "I still have to go out there and execute the golf shots. I'm just going to go out and try to shoot a good number and get ready for Sunday."
Even if he does not want to admit it publicly, Woods is also embarking on a historic journey towards golf greatness.
He demonstrated that by following an opening-round 70, which he produced in some very difficult conditions, with a six-under-par 66 that was the best round of the tournament.

Woods, who has a chance of becoming the youngest Masters champion by a difference of almost two years, combined awesome length and a deft putting touch with some imaginative shot making to put his name atop Augusta's famous leaderboards.
"I played strategically," Woods said of his almost flawless 66, in which he made only one bogey -- and that was on a par-four where he almost drove the green.
Woods also got some fortuitous help from the huge galleries that have surrounded him all week.
Asked what impact the adoring fans have on him, he said instantly: "Number one, they're stopping a couple of my shots."

He was referring to his par save on the ninth hole, where he drove into the trees on the left and then hooked a seven-iron into the gallery surrounding the green, which blocked his ball just off the green and allowed him to two-putt for par.
But that incident should not be misinterpreted. Woods may be lucky at times, like all golfers, but in reality he is good, very good.
He is so good that, to describe him, perhaps the greatest living golfer had to evoke the immortal words of perhaps the greatest golfer ever.

In 1965, when Jack Nicklaus won the first of his six Masters green jackets with a still record total of 271, Bobby Jones, the founder of the Masters and the last golfer to complete the game's Grand Slam, said of the 25-year-old Nicklaus: "He plays a game with which I am not familiar."

"It is a shame that Bobby Jones isn't here," Nicklaus said on Friday. "He could have saved the superlatives he used for me for this young man, because he certainly plays a game with which we are not familiar."
